subject: Clarify DPA role ownership and export evidence needed
messages:
From: Sara Jennings <sara.j@clientcorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clientcorp.com
Date: 2027-09-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: controller/processor split and export evidence needed

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal ran a quick scan of the MSA + Order Form and flagged a couple of items we need clarified before procurement can finish the purchase order:

1) Controller vs. processor — the DPA currently reads like Redwood is a processor, but some order-form language implies joint responsibilities for export controls. We need explicit language that clarifies roles and any processor obligations to assist with export notices.

2) SCCs + transfer evidence — because we'll route some EU-origin data to our APAC region during testing, our privacy team needs a list of evidence items (hosting locations, subprocessor roster, KMS zone) and whether Redwood will sign the SCCs as-is or propose a controller-side addendum.

Can you share a redline or checklist we can use in our legal review? Procurement also asked for any timing constraints — we prefer to close by end of month.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jennings
Senior Counsel, ClientCorp
Attachments: (none)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jennings <sara.j@clientcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: controller/processor split and export evidence needed

Sara —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a focused redline (Redlined_DPA_v3.docx) and a short SCCs evidence checklist (SCCs_Evidence_Checklist.pdf) that map back to the Order Form. High-level responses below and then a couple of asks for our internal legal/ops team:

- Controller/Processor: Redwood's default position for hosted customers is Processor; we include assistance-language in Exhibit B to support controller obligations (e.g., routing/export notices, records). Where the Order Form introduces controller responsibilities, we typically add a short carveout in the DPA to avoid conflicting obligations.

- SCCs: we can execute standard EU SCCs. If ClientCorp needs a transfer-impact addendum for APAC routing, we can offer an addendum — but we need confirmation of hosting regions and whether ClientCorp will opt into a transfer addendum or accept Redwood's standard SCC annex.

- Evidence: the checklist includes hosting zones, current subprocessor list, KMS region, SOC2 abstract (summary), and export routing diagram. Note: for MSP-hosted or private deployments this list expands.

Internal asks to Ben/Laura/Olga — can you: 1) review the redline and confirm whether the proposed carveout below (section marked [RDW: processor carveout]) is defensible for hosted customers, and 2) advise whether Redwood should proactively offer a transfer-impact addendum for APAC routing (ClientCorp prefers to close by 30 Sep).

I've flagged the MSA/Order Form tieouts in the spreadsheet (MSA_OrderForm_Tieouts.xlsx). Sara — if you can confirm the hosting regions and whether this will be a hosted or dedicated deployment, we'll finalize the addendum draft.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redlined_DPA_v3.docx (redline), SCCs_Evidence_Checklist.pdf (checklist), MSA_OrderForm_Tieouts.xlsx (mapping)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Sara Jennings <sara.j@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: controller/processor split and export evidence needed

Team —

Quick notes from legal redline review (see inline comments in Redlined_DPA_v3.docx):

1) Processor carveout: the proposed paragraph (under section 3) that limits processor duties when the Order Form assigns controller obligations is acceptable for hosted API customers. Wording recommends 'reasonable assistance' with a defined SLA for evidence requests (48–72 hours for routine items, longer for forensic requests).

2) SCCs acceptance: we can sign standard SCCs. For APAC routing, recommend offering a short transfer-impact addendum that:
   - confirms hosting regions and KMS zones;
   - includes a limited subprocessor notification window (7 days before onboarding);
   - preserves Redwood's right to fallback to compatible model variants if hosting constraints arise.

3) Evidence scope: add 'encrypted key access logs' to the checklist and confirm whether ClientCorp needs continuous export logs or a one-time export routing diagram. Continuous logs are operationally heavier — flagging as an ops cost.

If procurement needs signoff before 30 Sep, we should: 1) finalize the short addendum (I can draft), 2) supply the SCCs checklist and KMS region statements, and 3) record the items in HubSpot (linked).

Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redlined_DPA_v3.docx (annotated)
From: Sara Jennings <sara.j@clientcorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clientcorp.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: controller/processor split and export evidence needed

Naomi / Ben —

Thanks — this is helpful and moves us forward. Confirming: ClientCorp will proceed with hosted deployment in US + APAC test region (Sydney), and procurement is comfortable with a short transfer-impact addendum that confirms hosting + KMS zones.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Final addendum draft (to be reviewed by our privacy team)
- SCCs to sign (or pointer to signed SCCs if you execute on behalf of customers)
- The evidence checklist filled (we'd like the KMS region and current subprocessor list by COB Fri 24 Sep)

Once we have the addendum and evidence, I'll open the DocuSign envelope and loop procurement. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/7654321 (I've added the PO there).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement still hopes to close this month.

Best,
Sara
Senior Counsel, ClientCorp
